newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: No decision on early Metway exit - Queensland.
newsitem.headline: No decision on early Metway exit - Queensland.

text.p: The Queensland state government said it had made no decision on an early unwinding of its 67 percent stake in the Suncorp-Metway Ltd mega-bank.

"The government has made no decision on an early exit strategy. We have given a commitment to sell down within five years and we are sticking to that commitment," a spokesman for State treasurer Joan Sheldon told Reuters.
The spokesman's statement followed media reports that the government was planning to sell down its stake earlier in the light of a rising Metway Bank Ltd share price.

The state government retained its stake in a combined Suncorp-Metway-Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) bank following a May 1996 proposal under which Metway acquired QIDC and Suncorp from the government.
In return, the government was issued shares in the merged group with an undertaking to sell down to a 15 percent stake within five years.
Metway shareholders will vote on March 14 for a proposal to change the group's name to Suncorp-Metway Ltd.
Metway shares were trading two cents higher at A$5.59 at 2.20 p.m. (0320 GMT), nearer their 12-month high of A$6 than their low of A$3.87.
